## Zoom G3Xn "Princeton Warm" Patch Checklist

Guitar: MIJ Tele, neck pickup, volume/tone slightly rolled back Amp: Fender Blues Jr III (miked — no Zoom amp/cab sim used) Goal: warm, articulate Princeton Reverb-style clean tone with shimmer trem and spring reverb

## Signal Chain

Guitar → RackComp → RC Boost → Tremolo → FD Spring → Zoom output → Blues Jr input → mic

## Block 1 — RackComp (DYNAMICS)

- [ ] THRSH: 25–30
- [ ] Ratio: 3–4:1
- [ ] ATTCK: 5–6 (mid-slow, lets pick transient through before compressing)
- [ ] VOL: 100 (unity — no boost here)

## Block 2 — RC Boost (DRIVE)

- [ ] Gain: 15–20 (just enough to nudge the amp, not add drive character)
- [ ] Bass: 50
- [ ] Treble: 55–60
- [ ] VOL: 105–110 (small push, +2–4 dB feel)

## Block 3 — Tremolo (MODULATION)

- [ ] Wave: **TUBE**
- [ ] Depth: 35–40
- [ ] Rate: 30–35
- [ ] VOL: 100

## Block 4 — FD Spring (REVERB)

- [ ] Color: try 0 first, switch to 1 if thin
- [ ] Lo: 55–60
- [ ] Hi: 45–50
- [ ] Mix: 30–35

Alternative if FD Spring sounds too metallic: swap in plain **Spring** - PreD: 10–15 - Decay: 12–15 - Mix: 30–35

## Amp Settings — Blues Jr III

- [ ] Volume: 4–5
- [ ] Fat: OFF
- [ ] Treble: 5.5–6
- [ ] Bass: 4.5–5
- [ ] Middle: 5–6
- [ ] Master: 4–4.5
- [ ] Reverb: OFF or very low (FD Spring on the Zoom is handling reverb — avoid stacking two reverbs)

## Mic Setup — Blue Yeti (on stock desktop stand, floor placement)

- [ ] Mode: Cardioid
- [ ] Orientation: **logo side of mesh grille facing the amp** (this is the capsule's listening face — confirmed correct)
- [ ] Distance: 4–5 inches from grille
- [ ] Position: base shifted slightly to the **right** of the amp's centerline (creates true off-axis angle, since the stock stand doesn't swivel sideways)
- [ ] Tilt: forward, toward the amp — this aims the capsule up to cone height (compensating for the stand sitting lower than the speaker on the floor)
- [ ] Gain: set using the *loudest* tremolo peak, target -12 to -6 dB, no clipping

Notes: - Forward tilt = vertical aim adjustment (reaches cone height), not the off-axis angle - Sideways base offset = true off-axis angle (softens pick attack/harshness) - Both adjustments are used together in this floor setup since the stand can't swivel independently

## Test Pass

- [ ] Record 15–20 seconds of comping/chords
- [ ] RC Boost check: should be inaudible as a "pedal" — felt as amp push, not as added grit. If gritty, lower Gain further.
- [ ] Reverb check: confirm only FD Spring is audible, not doubled with Blues Jr reverb
- [ ] Tremolo check: TUBE wave should feel smoother/rounder than a standard triangle wave trem
- [ ] Compression check: RackComp should be felt as sustain/evenness, not obvious pumping
- [ ] Overall: does the amp feel like it's "working" a little (natural compression) rather than stiff/clean?
- [ ] If still too clean/stiff: raise Master first, before touching EQ
